reason: The supplied baseline scores remain below 1,800 GFLOP/s, and the measured panel, traversal, packed-B, and other candidates did not show a repeatable gain. I rank bounded K-loop prefetch first because it is a distinct, localized hypothesis with lower correctness risk, though its benefit is unverified. Panel packing and transpose fusion could reduce scratch traffic, but both change data movement substantially; transpose fusion also repeats work across output panels. Address generation is a narrow change, but prior pointer-end testing did not establish a gain. The proposed two-K loop simplification and ZA remapping have weak expected benefit; the loop simplification also conflicts with the supplied history that already measured a two-step loop. Tail alignment and general-path transpose fusion do not address the n=512 target.
